content: The use of IMITREX Nasal Spray is contraindicated in patients with ischemic or vasospastic coronary artery disease (CAD). Rare cases of serious cardiac adverse reactions, including acute myocardial infarction, have been reported within hours of administration, even in patients without known CAD. IMITREX Nasal Spray can induce coronary artery vasospasm (Prinzmetal’s angina), even in patients without a history of CAD. Patients with risk factors for CAD (e.g., age, diabetes, hypertension, smoking, obesity, or a strong family history of CAD) should undergo a cardiovascular evaluation prior to receiving IMITREX Nasal Spray. If CAD or coronary artery vasospasm is detected, the use of IMITREX Nasal Spray is contraindicated. For patients with multiple cardiovascular risk factors but a negative cardiovascular evaluation, consider administering the first dose in a medically supervised setting with an electrocardiogram (ECG) performed immediately after administration. Periodic cardiovascular evaluations should be considered for long-term intermittent users of IMITREX Nasal Spray. Life-threatening cardiac arrhythmias, including ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation leading to death, have been reported within hours of administration of 5-HT1 agonists. IMITREX Nasal Spray should be discontinued if such arrhythmias occur. It is contraindicated in patients with Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome or arrhythmias associated with other cardiac accessory conduction pathway disorders. Chest, throat, neck, and/or jaw pain, tightness, or pressure may occur after treatment with IMITREX Nasal Spray. These sensations are usually non-cardiac in origin, but a cardiac evaluation should be performed in patients at high cardiac risk. IMITREX Nasal Spray is contraindicated in patients with CAD or Prinzmetal’s variant angina. Cerebrovascular events, including cerebral hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and stroke, have occurred in patients treated with 5-HT1 agonists, some of which have been fatal. In some cases, these events were primary, with the 5-HT1 agonist administered under the mistaken belief that the symptoms were due to migraine. IMITREX Nasal Spray should be discontinued if a cerebrovascular event occurs. Before treating headaches in patients not previously diagnosed with migraines or in migraineurs presenting with atypical symptoms, other potentially serious neurological conditions should be excluded. IMITREX Nasal Spray is contraindicated in patients with a history of stroke or transient ischemic attack (TIA). IMITREX Nasal Spray may cause non-coronary vasospastic reactions, such as peripheral vascular ischemia, gastrointestinal vascular ischemia and infarction (manifesting as abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea), splenic infarction, and Raynaud’s syndrome. In patients experiencing symptoms suggestive of non-coronary vasospasm following the use of a 5-HT1 agonist, a vasospastic reaction should be ruled out before further use of IMITREX Nasal Spray. Reports of transient and permanent blindness, as well as significant partial vision loss, have been associated with 5-HT1 agonists. While visual disturbances may be part of a migraine attack, a causal relationship with 5-HT1 agonists has not been definitively established. Medication overuse headache (MOH) may occur in patients using ergotamine, triptans, opioids, or a combination of these drugs for 10 or more days per month. MOH may present as daily migraine-like headaches or a marked increase in migraine frequency. Detoxification, including withdrawal of the overused drugs and management of withdrawal symptoms (which may include a transient worsening of headache), may be necessary. Serotonin syndrome, a potentially life-threatening condition, has been reported with the use of serotonergic medications. Symptoms typically occur within minutes to hours of receiving a new or higher dose of a serotonergic drug. IMITREX Nasal Spray should be discontinued if serotonin syndrome is suspected. Significant elevations in blood pressure, including hypertensive crisis with acute organ system impairment, have been reported in patients treated with 5-HT1 agonists, even in those without a history of hypertension. Blood pressure should be monitored in patients receiving IMITREX Nasal Spray. It is contraindicated in patients with uncontrolled hypertension. Local irritation, such as burning, numbness, paresthesia, discharge, and pain or soreness, was reported in approximately 5% of patients in controlled clinical trials, with severe symptoms in about 1%. These symptoms were transient and generally resolved within two hours. Limited examinations of the nose and throat did not reveal clinically significant injury. The effects of extended and repeated use of IMITREX Nasal Spray on nasal and/or respiratory mucosa have not been systematically evaluated. Anaphylactic or anaphylactoid reactions have occurred in patients receiving IMITREX. These reactions can be life-threatening or fatal. Individuals with a history of sensitivity to multiple allergens are at higher risk for anaphylactic reactions to drugs. IMITREX Nasal Spray is contraindicated in patients with a history of hypersensitivity to IMITREX. Seizures have been reported following the administration of IMITREX. Some occurred in patients with a history of seizures or concurrent conditions predisposing to seizures, while others occurred in patients without apparent predisposing factors. IMITREX Nasal Spray should be used with caution in patients with a history of epilepsy or conditions associated with a lowered seizure threshold.
